questions.question:
An administrator wants to configure dead peer detection (DPD) on IPsec VPN for detecting dead tunnels. The requirement is that FortiGate sends DPD probes only when there is no inbound traffic.
Which DPD mode on FortiGate meets this requirement?
answers: A. Enabled
B. On Idle
C. Disabled
D. On Demand

comments.content:
The DPD mode on FortiGate that meets the requirement of sending DPD probes only when there is no inbound traffic is On Idle.

The correct answer is B. On Idle.

FortiGate DPD Modes Explained
On Idle → This mode sends DPD probes when no traffic (inbound or outbound) is detected on the tunnel for a configured period. This directly addresses the requirement of detecting a dead tunnel when no inbound traffic is present.

Enabled → This mode sends DPD probes periodically, regardless of traffic activity.

Disabled → DPD is completely turned off.

On Demand → This mode sends a DPD probe only when the FortiGate needs to send traffic but the Phase 2 tunnel is not yet up. This is usually to initiate the connection.
Hi, has someone already sit this exam? If yes tell me how it went. Thanks.

Dead Peer Detection (DPD) in FortiGate has several modes, and the requirement is to send DPD probes only when there is no inbound traffic.

    A. Enabled: Sends DPD probes at regular intervals, regardless of traffic. (Does not meet the requirement.)

    B. On Idle: Sends DPD probes only when no traffic is detected for a certain time. (Fits the requirement perfectly.)

    C. Disabled: No DPD probes are sent. (Does not meet the requirement.)

    D. On Demand: Sends DPD probes only when needed (but not strictly tied to inbound traffic absence). (Less precise than "On Idle.")

Thus, "On Idle" (B) is the correct mode for sending DPD probes only when there is no inbound traffic.
FortiGate solo envía sondas DPD cuando no hay tráfico entrante.
On Demand : "FortiGate sends DPD probes if there is only outbound traffic through the tunnel, but no inbound."

About DPD on IPsec VPN :

Disable: Disable Dead Peer Detection.
On-idle: Trigger Dead Peer Detection when no IPsec traffic is received.
On-demand: Trigger Dead Peer Detection when no IPsec traffic is received AND FortiGate has been sending IPsec traffic. On-demand is the default setting.

B is Correct!

Study Guide Page 380 - Phase 1—Network—Dead Peer Detection (DPD)
Three modes:
• On Demand: DPD probes are sent when there is no inbound traffic
* • On Idle: DPD probes are sent when there is no traffic *
• Disabled: only reply to DPD probes—don’t send probes

questions.question: Which three statements explain a flow-based antivirus profile? (Choose three.)
answers: A. FortiGate buffers the whole file but transmits to the client at the same time.
B. Flow-based inspection uses a hybrid of the scanning modes available in proxy-based inspection.
C. If a virus is detected, the last packet is delivered to the client.
D. Flow-based inspection optimizes performance compared to proxy-based inspection.
E. The IPS engine handles the process as a standalone.

comments.content:
A is correct

The IPS Engine buffers the packets and sends them to the client at the same time
When the last packet arrives, the IPS engine buffers it, but do not send it to the client
Upon arrival of the last packet, it reassembles the data and send it to the Antivirus Engine for scanning
If the Antivirus Engines reports back that the data is clean, the IPS Engine sends the last packet to client
If Antivirus Engine said virus exists, the IPS engine sends reset packet to the client instead of the last packet 




E is wrong

The IPS Engine does not handle the process all by itself stand alone
It sends the assembled data to the Antivirus Engine for scanning
Corrects answers are B, D , E

B is correct : Flow-based mode combines some of the detection techniques of proxy-based mode, but operates at the flow level rather than the full session level.

D is correct : Flow-based mode is more efficient because it analyzes packets “on the fly” without having to buffer the entire file, unlike proxy-based

E is correct : In flow-based mode, it is the FortiGate IPS engine that also manages the antivirus functions, so the processing is done in this engine, without the proxy.

A is incorrect : This is the behavior of proxy-based mode, not flow-based.

questions.question:
You are analyzing connectivity problems caused by intermediate devices blocking traffic in SSL VPN environment.
In which two ways can you effectively resolve the problem? (Choose two.)
answers: A. You can turn off IKE fragmentation to fix large certificate negotiation problems.
B. You should use IPsec to solve issues with fragment drops and large certificate exchanges.
C. You can use SSL VPN tunnel mode to prevent problems with blocked ESP and UDP ports (500 or 4500).
D. You can configure a hub-and-spoke topology with SSL VPN tunnels to bypass blocked UDP ports.

comments.content:
Question is misleading, C & D are listed in the Training material

The training is basically trying to point out the advantage of FortiGate's SSL VPN over IPSec VPN in situation where issues are caused by an intermediate device 

C - IPsec uses ESP and UDP 500 and 4500, so where these are blocked, SSL VPN tunnel mode shines because it uses HTTPS (443) and TLS by default (both TCP)

D - Again where UDP ports are blocked, SSL VPN shines (Tunnel mode Hub and Spoke) because it does not use UDP

A & B - IKE Fragmentation is an IPSec VPN thing, and yes if an intermediate device is dropping packets because of fragmentation, the solution is to turn it off under the IKE phase configuration - this is does not happen is SSL VPN

Even though it says IKE fragmentation, Fortinet’s current exam guide uses it in a generic sense:

“Disable IKE fragmentation” → “avoid packet fragmentation during large certificate exchanges.”

Some intermediate devices break connections when packet fragmentation occurs during SSL or IKE negotiations.
Therefore, disabling fragmentation can prevent large certificate packets from being dropped in transit.

👉 In summary, even though IKE is part of IPsec, Fortinet considers that the same logic of avoiding fragmentation also applies to SSL VPN environments, which is why option A is valid in the 7.6 exam.
The statement makes more sense if instead of saying “SSL VPN” it said “IPsec VPN.” As stated, none of the options is optimal. If the statement said IPsec VPN, then options A and C would be correct.

B. FortiGate entered into IPS fail open state.
C. Administrator entered the command diagnose test application ipsmonitor 5.
D. Administrator entered the command diagnose test application ipsmonitor 99.

comments.content:
The exhibit shows the output of the FortiGate command `diagnose test application ipsmonitor 1`.

The output is:

```
pid = 2044, engine count = 0 (+1)
0 - pid:2074:2074 cfg:1 master:0 run:1
```

The key piece of information here is: **`engine count = 0 (+1)`**

This output indicates that the FortiGate is not currently running any **IPS engine worker processes**. It shows a count of `0` engines, with an intent to start `(+1)` engine for the test.

In a normal operational state, a FortiGate will start a number of IPS engines based on the number of available CPU cores (if IPS is enabled in a policy). If the IPS engine count drops to zero, it often suggests that the FortiGate has stopped the IPS inspection process for an emergency reason, which is usually a state known as **IPS fail-open**.

The correct reason for this output is:

**B. FortiGate entered into IPS fail open state.**
A. There is a no firewall policy configured with an IPS security profile.

questions.question: What is the primary FortiGate election process when the HA override setting is enabled?
answers: A. Connected monitored ports > Priority > HA uptime > FortiGate serial number
B. Connected monitored ports > Priority > System uptime > FortiGate serial number
C. Connected monitored ports > HA uptime > Priority > FortiGate serial number
D. Connected monitored ports > System uptime > Priority > FortiGate serial number

comments.content: when the HA override setting is enabled on a FortiGate cluster, the primary unit election process changes significantly. the goal of this setting is to ensure that a specific pre-determined FortiGate unit becomes the primary, even if another unit has been online for longer. essentially enabling HA override forces the cluster to prioritize the device priority setting above all other tie-breakers except the number of connected monitored interfaces. this is to ensure the unit with the highest priority is always the primary, which is useful for situations like firmware upgrades where you want a specific unit to take over

Primary unit selection criteria when override is enabled (MPUS):
The device that has a higher number of operationally UP Monitored interfaces (M).
 The device that has the highest Priority (P).
A device that has the highest HA Uptime, not the unit uptime (U)
The device that has the highest Serial Number (S).

https://community.fortinet.com/t5/FortiGate/Technical-Tip-FortiGate-HA-Primary-unit-selection-process-when/ta-p/249745

Override Enabled: MPUS (highest Monitored ports, Priority, ha Uptime, Serial nr)
Override Disabled: MUPS (highest Monitored ports, ha Uptime, Priority, Serial nr)
https://community.fortinet.com/t5/FortiGate/Technical-Tip-FortiGate-HA-Primary-unit-selection-process-when/ta-p/249745

When HA override is enabled, the FortiGate HA election process follows this order:

    Connected monitored ports – The device with the most monitored interfaces up becomes primary.

    Priority – If monitored ports are equal, the higher priority (lower numerical value) wins.

    System uptime – If priority is equal, the unit with the longer uptime becomes primary.

    FortiGate serial number – Used as a tiebreaker if all else is equal.

Why the other options are incorrect:

    A & C incorrectly include "HA uptime" (not a factor in the election process).

    D reverses Priority and System uptime, which is incorrect.

Correct Answer: B
